content_metadata.description: An animated educational video exploring the concept of sustainability and its three pillars: environment, economics, and social progress, culminating in a call to action for viewers to contribute towards a sustainable future.

qAndA.question: What animal is shown as an example of being affected by climate change?
What item is used to demonstrate the interconnectedness of the world through global trade?
What type of energy sources are mentioned as sustainable alternatives to oil and coal?
What organization's plan for sustainable development is mentioned in the video?

qAndA.answer: The video starts with a playful and carefree mood, then transitions to a more serious and informative tone as the topic of sustainability is introduced. Later, a sense of hope and excitement emerges as the video presents solutions and calls for action towards a sustainable future.
qAndA.question: How does the mood of the video shift throughout the different scenes?

activities.description: Sitting on the Earth, looking at each other.

characterInteraction.description: Girl 1 and Boy 1 seem to be friends, comfortable in each other's presence.

narrativeProgression.description: Introduction of the setting and the main characters.

videoEditingDetails.description: Animated transition into the scene with Earth appearing from a black hole.

activities.description: Girl 1 and Boy 1 sitting on Earth, looking at the camera.
Transitioning to different illustrations related to sustainability.

characterInteraction.description: Girl 1 and Boy 1 become listeners, engaging with the narrator's questions.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The Earth shown with damages emphasizes the negative impacts of unsustainable practices.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The music becomes more serious, reflecting the shift in tone from playful to informative.

narrativeProgression.description: The narrator raises questions about sustainability and its importance. Three pillars of sustainable development are introduced.

props.name: Earth (partially damaged), question marks, illustrations depicting social progress, economic development, and climate and environment.

scenes.thematicElements: Sustainability, environmental responsibility, social responsibility, economic responsibility
scenes.title: Embrace of Sustainability Concept

videoEditingDetails.description: Fast cuts between illustrations. Animated transition between different aspects of sustainability.

characterInteraction.description: The monkey briefly appears, embodying the vulnerable wildlife.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The monkey's X-ray image turning to a skeleton symbolizes the potential extinction of species due to unsustainable practices.

narrativeProgression.description: The narrator explains the importance of protecting natural ecosystems and the climate system.
Focus shifts to responsible use of natural resources and sustainable energy sources.

props.name: Rainforest, polar bear, factory, cityscape, ocean with oil rigs, windmills, solar panels.

scenes.thematicElements: Environmental protection, climate change, renewable energy, resource management, sustainable economic practices.
scenes.title: Exploration of Environmental Sustainability

videoEditingDetails.description: Animated transitions between different environmental scenes. Visual representation of greenhouse gas emissions and their effect.

activities.description: Illustrating economic aspects of sustainability through resource distribution and trade.
Illustrating social progress as a key factor in sustainable development.

characterInteraction.description: The scientist appears, symbolizing the role of knowledge and innovation.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The football's journey across the globe signifies the interconnectedness of countries and economies.

narrativeProgression.description: The narrator uses the journey of a football to illustrate the complexities of global trade.
The focus shifts to the importance of social progress.

props.name: Football, train, sewing machine, factory, classroom, hospital bed, school, notebook, lightbulb, drawing of an alien.

scenes.thematicElements: Global trade, fair trade, resource distribution, education, healthcare, social equality, innovation.
scenes.title: Economic and Social Aspects of Sustainability

videoEditingDetails.description: Animated transitions following the journey of a football from its production to its final use.

activities.description: Summarizing the three pillars of sustainable development.
Emphasizing the need for cooperation and individual action.

characterInteraction.description: Girl 1 and Boy 1 reappear on a screen in the space station, symbolizing the future generation.

scenes.contextualRelevance: The characters and space station symbolize a future where sustainable development is embraced.

keyMoments.changeDescription: The music shifts back to an upbeat and optimistic tone.

narrativeProgression.description: The narrator reiterates the importance of all three pillars of sustainability working together.
The focus shifts to the United Nations' joint plan for sustainable development and the need for global cooperation.

props.name: Earth, futuristic space station control room, TV screen displaying Girl 1 and Boy 1 on Earth.

scenes.thematicElements: Global cooperation, United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, call to action, individual responsibility.
scenes.title: Conclusion and Call to Action

videoEditingDetails.description: Animated transition back to the characters on Earth, zooming into a futuristic space station.

climax.description: Visually demonstrating the interconnectedness of the world through the football's journey.

storylines.description: An exploration of sustainability through its three pillars, leading to a call to action.

content_metadata.title: Sustaining Our Future: A Journey Through Sustainability

trimmingSuggestions.description: The repeated visual of the three circles representing sustainability could be shortened.
The extended sequence showing the lava flow and the island formation could be trimmed slightly to maintain a faster pace.

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi guys!
Do you have time for a few quick questions?
I see you're having a lot of fun.
But do you ever stop and think if what you do is sustainable?
And do you know what sustainable development means?
Sustainable development is to make the world a better place for everyone now
without destroying the possibilities for the next generations.
If you wonder if something is sustainable you can ask yourself,
can we do this over and over again forever?
Sustainable development means that we need to keep three things in mind at once.
Social progress, economic development, and climate and environment.
First of all, we have to take care of our planet.
We have many natural ecosystems that must be in balance in order for us to live here.
The climate system is one of them.
This system ensures that the temperature is correct and that the atmosphere emits exactly the right amount of solar energy.
When we emit harmful greenhouse gases such as CO2, we clog the atmosphere.
This changes the temperatures and earth which again affects our development.
How we produce and use energy is incredibly important.
Oil and coal are examples of energy we may run out of.
Water, wind, and sun, however, will always be here.
Using the lasting sources of energy that renew themselves is good for the planet
and can provide jobs for years to come.
Economics.
Almost everything we develop by and trade starts with nature.
The smarter we use our natural resources and the better systems we create for our fair distribution, the more sustainable we are.
One way to contribute to a more and even distribution is to be more aware of what we buy and how it is produced.
A football is a good example.
It travels far before it reaches the football players.
First, materials are made.
Then, they print the logo somewhere else.
Before a third country sees it all together.
One single football sees the whole world before it reaches its goal.
This journey ties us together.
If we are to win the battle for a sustainable future, we have to play with fair rules that apply to everyone.
Social progress.
We humans are part of nature, but we are also important resources for the world.
Just like water, the forest, and the sun.
We have minds that can create the strangest and most creative things.
But for us to be the best versions of ourselves, there are certain things that must be in order.
Like having equal opportunities to education, safety, food, and medicine.
This provides greater opportunities for us as human beings.
But also for the planet, we just have to think in new ways.
These three must work together.
That is sustainable development.
And there is actually a plan for this.
All the countries of the United Nations have agreed on a joint plan for sustainable development.
But for the plan to work, we need to cooperate and we need you to be on board.
Are you with us?
You

youtube_description:
A simple introduction to sustainable development and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The film is produced by Animaskin on behalf of UN Association of Norway and UNICEF Norway, as part of an interdisciplinary learning program for students on primary and secondary level.

Read more about this topic at https://www.fn.no/Undervisning/Baerekraft and https://www.unicef.no/skole/barekraft
